variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: a modular head sprite for the Gobble avatar editor, NOT a complete avatar.
Input image: the supplied blank head PNG is the edit target and exact drawing/framing reference.
Keep the square canvas, transparent margins, pose, skin palette, warm peach shading, upper-left lighting, softly illustrated cartoon finish and clean outline of this reference. Keep the crown at approximately y=120/1024, chin at y=640/1024, central axis x=512/1024. Keep the ears in their existing places. The head occupies only its original small central upper portion of the square canvas; do not enlarge, recenter vertically or crop it. The forehead and eye region must keep the same alignment to fit existing overlay pieces: eyes centers (430,390) and (594,390), nose base y470, mouth y535 on the 1024 authoring grid.
The central face remains completely featureless: NO eyes, eyelids, eyebrows, nose, mouth, lips, hair, facial hair, neck, clothes or accessories. Do not add text, labels, frames or a checkerboard pattern. Keep a genuinely transparent background and clean native alpha edges. Output one single square transparent PNG head only.
Requested change ONLY: create the masculine FIN / MAIGRE version. Make the lower face visibly slimmer and leaner than the reference, through an actual changed silhouette: gently hollowed cheeks below the eye line, tapered lower cheeks and a narrower jaw and chin (roughly 15 percent slimmer lower face). Preserve the original forehead width and cranium and the eye region so the existing large eyes fit. The cheek hollows should have subtle soft shading, not deep carved wrinkles. The result should read as a naturally slender face, with a calm smooth youthful skin surface, not an old or skeletal face. No ageing creases, no nasolabial lines, no sickly dark circles. Keep the chin at the same vertical level and ears aligned exactly as the reference. Preserve the masculine slightly angular character of this base.

On the 1024 authoring frame the future eyes are centered at x430/y390 and x594/y390, their outer corners approximately x367/y402 and x657/y402. Add just two short fine softly shaded lines fanning outward into the temple on each side, mainly in x340-370/y396-418 and x654-684/y396-418. These are subtle expression lines, enough to read in an avatar but far lighter than an elderly wrinkled face. Everything else stays smooth: absolutely NO forehead wrinkles, frown lines, under-eye bags, deep eye sockets, cheek creases, nasolabial folds, chin folds or sagging skin. Do NOT draw the eyes or any other facial features. Only the two tiny crow's-feet groups on the otherwise blank original face.
